hyperMILL
1 New in version 2018.1

New in version 2018.1

     Project Assistant

                         Use the Project Assistant to create a milling or MillTurn project step by step and in a simple
                         and clear manner. Information in section Creating a milling project / MillTurn project with the
                         Project Assistant.

     Name pattern for jobs and comments

                                 Define the names of jobs or comments individually and automatically by selecting job param-
                                 eters. Information in section Using name patterns for jobs and comments.

     Toolpath quickinfo

                                 Information is available for the following via a quickinfo (tooltip): frame, job ID, job name,
                                 comment, job type, linked job, tool ID and tool name. For further information, see section
                                 Information on calculated toolpaths.

     New cycle: Rollfeed Turning
                                 Machine turning parts by rolling the tool insert on the component contour.

     2D Contour Milling on 3D Model

                                 Contour definition via a surface selection. Information in section Contour Milling on 3D
                                 Model.

     3D Optimised Roughing
                                 Optimised machining of adaptive pockets with large lateral but small vertical infeed and high
                                 feedrate.
                                 · Automatic calculation of the lateral infeed based on the defined scallop height.
                                 · It is also possible to define the scallop height for plane level detection.
                                 · Smooth rolling in of the tool in the adaptive pocket area.
                                 Information in section Strategy.
                                 Feedrate reduction during full cut is also now available for 3D Optimised Roughing. Informa-
                                 tion in section Strategy.

     Slope dependent machining
                                 Use the Smooth overlap option to optimise the surface quality in the transition area between
                                 flat and steep areas with small retract movements of the tool. Available for the following
                                 cycles:
                                 · 3D Profile Finishing
                                 · 3D Complete Finishing
                                 · 3D Z Level Shape Finishing
                                 · 3D Z Level Finishing
                                 Information in section Strategy.

     Feature technology

                                 Contour feature: The Point option is now also available as a contour parameter (type). This
                                 provides improved automation during machining probing. Information in section Contour.

     Tool database

                         Extended coolant management

                         Define up to seven further coolants in addition to the standard coolants. A unique, consecu-
                         tive ID is allocated to each coolant. This makes an evaluation possible during the postproc-
                         essor run. Additional information (coolant properties, coolant type) can be allocated to a
                         coolant.

1-2                                                                                                          hyperMILL
           New in version 2018.1  1                                                                                                     1 New in version 2018.1

           Simulation             Couplings
                                  The top coupling is no longer defined for the tool but is now defined for the holder. The cou-
                                  pling remains visible for the tool but cannot be edited.
                                  The Adaptor coupling type can now also be combined with tool holders and extensions.

                                  New tool: roll turn tool
                                  The new Roll turn tool, tool type is available in the new Rollfeed Turning cycle. Four different
                                  insert types are available for the roll turn tool to ensure an optimal rolling of the tool insert on
                                  the component contour.

                                  New inserts
                                  Four new insert types can be defined for the roll turn tool:
                                  · X Full Roll Turn
                                  · X Short Roll Turn
                                  · T Full Roll Turn
                                  · T Short Roll Turn

                                  X/Z setting length for turning tools
                                  Improved display of turning tools in the graphics area of the tool database by displaying the
                                  Setting length x and Setting length z for turning tools.

                                  External simulation
                                  Support of COLLISION SAFEGUARD as an external simulation program. Information in sec-
                                  tion External simulation.

                                  Improved rest material display
                                  Rest material is now displayed in four steps during the machine simulation. The steps are
                                  defined on the basis of the value of the maximum permissible rest material.
                                  Example: maximum rest material = 1. First step = <0.25, second step = < 0.5, third step = <
                                  0.75, fourth step = > 0.75.

          Overview

User interface

     Overview

                    This user's guide covers the CAM editing functions. For information on the CAD functions,
                    see the various online help texts (available on the Help menu).

     hyperMILL: Integrated CAM Application

                                The hyperMILL CAM solution requires you to have installed a working version of a CAD
                                application or the Geometric Engine from hyperMILL, into which it is fully integrated. It is
                                 used for generating 2D, 3D, 5-axis and turning NC programs for model and mold construc-
                                tion. hyperMILL is available as an integrated application for the following CAD systems:

                                · hyperCAD-S

                                · hyperCAD

                                 · Autodesk Inventor

                                 · SolidWorks

                                 Note that some of the functions described in this guide are not available in your installation.
                                 The range of functions depends on the licences obtained and the configuration of the soft-
                                 ware purchased.

     hyperMILL SHOP Viewer

                                The hyperMILL SHOP Viewer allows you to display, analyse and document processed CAD/
                                CAM data. The software works on the basis of hyperCAD-S and hyperMILL. The following
                                software documentation explains all the features of hyperMILL. The functions described may
                                not be available or may not be available to the extent described, in hyperMILL SHOP Viewer.

                                For further information on the functions of hyperMILL SHOP Viewer, please refer to the cor-
                                responding section in the product documentation for hyperCAD-S.

     Supported CAD formats

                                 Supports a wide range of geometry formats (e.g. DXF, DWG, IGES, VDA), which enable
                                 data exchange with the majority of CAD construction programs. Data conversion takes place
                                 in the background, while the model is loading.

                                 During conversion a log window with status information is displayed. The corresponding log
                                 file (*.log) can be opened and viewed later on from within the directory of the associated
                                 model file.

                    Direct interfaces are provided as modules for the following data formats: CATIA

                    V4, CATIA V5, PTC CREO, Siemens NX, Parasolid and SolidWorks. Please
                    contact your dealer. For more information, please see the product documenta-

                    tion for OPEN MIND direct interfaces.

3 Basics                                        Specify basic settings

Basics

            From the model to the NC program

                                             The modular structure of hyperMILL creates a flexible workflow from the model to the NC
                                               program. Important elements of this workflow include:

                                                                                 CAM/CAD system

          Specify basic settings

          Define workpiece origin and frame(s)  Define tool

          Prepare manufacturing geometry        Structure CAM projects
          (contours, surfaces, stockmodel)      (joblist, compound job, job)

          Collision check preparations

           Calculate toolpaths
          Simulate toolpaths

          Generate NC program

     Specify basic settings

                                Define the measurement system and storage directories for hyperMILL data. Configure the
                                 dialogue control, configure the tool and macro database and define further basic settings.
                                 Information in section Specify basic settings.

     Define workpiece origin and frame(s)

                                 With the origin reference system (NC system), establish a connection to the machine coordi-
                                 nate system. For information on the NC system, see section NC system and frames.
                                 Using a frame, define the current machining side and machining direction. See the informa-
                                 tion in section NC system and frames.
                                 To machine identical component areas, use transformations to reproduce and position tool-
                                 paths as required. See the information in section Transformations.

                                 Use origins to control the NC output and apply origins when defining transformations. See
                                 the information in section Origins.

           NC system and frames

           NC system  The NC system defines the position of the workpiece origin and the orientation of the
           Frame      machining axes (XYZ).
                      The workpiece origin must match the reference point of the workpiece on the machine.
                      hyperMILL calculates all the toolpaths in the NC system. The NC system applies to an entire                                         In hyperMILL, the first point of a toolpath can also lie below the level given by the height of
                      job list at one time.                                                                                                               the machining side in the z+ direction. This generally means below the uppermost point in
                                                                                                                                                          the model. The positioning movements made by the machine axes up to this first point are
                      A frame defines the current machining side and orientation. In multi-axis indexing, a frame                                         not represented in the toolpath, but defined in the postprocessor. An OPEN MIND postproc-
                      has to be defined for each machining side. The assignment of the frame to a job takes place                                         essor positions the rotational axes first, and only then proceeds to the first point of the tool-
                      in the job definition.
                      NC system (1)                                                                                                                       path along the linear axes. This needs to be taken into particular consideration during 5X
                      Frames (2-4)                                                                                                                        programming, for example when linking with the Clearance mode > Radial option or linking
                                                                                                                                                          triaxial toolpaths with differently oriented frames.

                                                                                                                                Define NC system

                                                                                                                                                            When a new (empty) joblist is opened, the NC system aligns with the world workplane.
                                                                                                                                                            Before a joblist is defined, the NC system must be adapted to the machining conditions.
                                                                                                                                                            These changes can be made via the joblist (Setup dialogue page) or the frame definition.

                                                                                                                                Define Frames                   In the hyperMILL browser, go to the Frames tab and use the New frame shortcut menu
                                                                                                                                                                or
                                                                                                                                                            1.

                                                                                                                                                          2.    click the icon in the job definition on the Tool dialogue page

                                                                                                                                Definition

                                     All frames must be defined before generating the toolpaths. Subsequent move-                                         Reference system
                                     ment or rotation will mean having to recalculate all tool paths affected by the                                      The frame origin coordinates are dependent on the reference system set here.
                                     change. If the NC system is modified, then the entire joblist has to be recalcu-
                                     lated. If frames are modified, the affected jobs must be recalculated.                                               Move
                                                                                                                                                          Move: Move the frame origin.
                      Correct job definition and therefore machining can be achieved only if the tool coordinate
                      system is in the correct position and orientation for the job, because:                                                             Align
                      All definitions for the vertical machining area are in relation to the frame (top, bottom), clear-                                  Reference, Workplane: Frame origin and orientation are adopted from the active reference
                      ance distance, XY plane, horizontal stepover.                                                                                       system or the workplane.
                                                                                                                                                          3 Points: Specify the frame orientation with three points. Point 1 = origin, Point 2 = X direc-
                      The frame shares responsibility for collision checking during machining.                                                            tion, Point 3 = Y direction.

                      Surfaces that cannot be recognised from the tool axis perspective (1) are not machined.                                             MillTurn

                                                                                                                                                             If you modify a frame later on, recheck all the jobs that use the frame.

                                                                                                                                                             A frame is not moved on a job-specific basis. Instead, the translation operations

                                                                                                                                                             use the frame.

                                                                                                                                   Origins

                                                                                                                                                             Influence your NC output by defining origins.

                                                                                                                                                             Make accuracy or tolerance corrections for a specific area of the part to be machined as well
                                                                                                                                                             as precise position adjustments.

                                                                                                                                                             Each zero point is identified by a unique ID. The ID is translated into NC instructions during
                                                                                                                                                             postprocessing using an origin table.

                                                                                                                                                             For more information on this, please contact your OPEN MIND partner.

                                                                                                                                                 Defining the manufacturing parameters
           Mirror                                                                                                                                Enable the Copy option to create a mirror of the original (job, compound job or job list). In the
                                                                                                                                                 hyperMILL browser, a mirrored copy of the original element is created and associatively
                     This special type of transformation mirrors the base geometry. The prerequisite for proper                                  linked with the original.
                     mirror application in hyperMILL is the symmetry of the workpiece in use.                                                    All parameters are therefore greyed out in the mirrored jobs and cannot be edited directly.
                                                                                                                                                 As a result of the direct link (associativity) between the original job and the mirrored copy, all
                     hyperMILL then calculates new toolpaths on the basis of the mirrored geometry.                                              changes to the original job are also taken into account in the copy during the recalculation.

                     Advantages                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        hyperMILL

                     · Full associativity between the base geometry and the mirrored element (job, compound
                           job or job list)

                     · No limitations for 2D, 3D and 5X machining

                     · Flexibility as a result of partial deactivation of the direct link between the base element
                           and the mirrored element

                     · Retention of technology parameters (such as auto climb, automatic macros or opti-
                           mised linking movements) in the mirror.

                     · Patterns can be combined.

                                                                                                                                                                     tool database from the shortcut menu. If the ID of the tool already exists in the external data-
                                                                                                                                                                     base, a dialogue box (Constraint Violation) is shown; here, the ID highlighted in red must be

                                                                                                                                                                     exists, the differences will be displayed in a dialogue box.

                                                                                                                                                              The database remains password- protected after a successful export. For a re-

           Create stock chain

                                       Use the Create stock chain function to create a resulting stock model for any job in a
                                       sequence of machining steps, based on the stock model of the preceding job and the tool-
                                       path of the current job. This function is available for joblists, any jobs in a joblist, an individual
                                       job or a compound job.
                                       Requirements: A start stockmodel must be present. All toolpaths of the jobs for which a
                                       stockmodel is to be created must have been calculated.
                                       Procedure:

                                      1. In the hyperMILL browser, select the jobs for which you want to create a stock chain.

                                       2. Select the Stock > Create stock chain function from the shortcut menu.

                                            hyperMILL creates a stock object in the stock browser for each of the selected jobs.

                                 3. To calculate the stockmodels, use the Stock > Calculate (update) function on the short-
                                       cut menu.

                                                  hyperMILL calculates the stockmodels for each of the generated stock objects. The
                                       stockmodels are indicated by a corresponding icon in the stock browser.

           Functions on the shortcut menu: Models (stockmodels)

                                       New stock / New compound stock: Generate a new (compound) stockmodel.
                                       Mirror stock: Generate a new stockmodel by mirroring the selected stockmodel.

           Compound job

                                       Organise your joblists with compound jobs and clearly structure extensive CAM projects.
                                       Use compound jobs to structure transformations or assign individual transformations to sev-
                                       eral jobs. In contrast to joblists, which only permit mirrors, compound jobs also allow linear
                                       patterns and circular patterns in addition to mirrors.

                                       For information on compound jobs, see section Compound job.

           Linking job

                        Link jobs with each other in such a way that approach and retract movements for the entire
                        machining sequence and all linking movements between the individual jobs can be opti-
                        mised and monitored for collisions.

                        For information on linking jobs, see section Linking job.

           NC event

                        Structure your programming, independent of joblists and jobs, with control-specific functions
                        and commands that are forwarded directly to the postprocessor.

                        For information on the NC event, see section NC event.

           Defining a joblist

                                       A job list is automatically created when you call up a machining cycle for a job definition.
                                      In order to create another joblist in the hyperMILL browser, switch to the Jobs tab, right-click
                                       New > select Joblist.

                                       Joblist settings can be defined separately for each joblist. You must make the settings before
                                       you calculate the toolpaths.

                                       To edit, double-click the joblist or select the Edit function from the shortcut menu.

           Exporting/importing a joblist

                                       Save a joblist with all its parameters and settings in *.jst format and transfer to other CAD
                                       models.

                                       Advantages: Job archiving is independent of the drawings, fast programming of frequently
                                       occurring procedures, transfer of jobs to workpieces with the same drawing parts when
                                       machining sequence is the same.

           Compound job                                                                                                                  Linking job   A linking job contains other jobs that can be linked with each other in such a way that
                                                                                                                                                       approach and retract movements for the entire machining sequence and all linking move-
                                       Compound jobs allow joblists to be structured clearly. You can combine any 2D, 3D or 5X           Advantages
                                       jobs into a compound job. For example, you can combine a machining section (roughing, fin-        Requirements  ments between the individual jobs can be optimised and monitored for collisions.
                                       ishing) into a compound job.

           Jobs                     Tools                    Frames                                                                                    · Shortened machining times.
                                                                                                                                                       · Option to perform complex machining tasks.
                                                                                                                                                       · Improved product flexibility.

                                    Workpiece_001_AM08                                                                                                 To combine multiple jobs into a linking job, the following conditions must be met:
                                    Roughing
                                    Z Level Finishing                                                                                                  2D/3D machining:
                                    Downward machining                                                                                                 · All sub-jobs use the same tool.
                                    Upward machining                                                                                                   · Only mirrors are permitted in the sub-jobs, not linear or circular patterns.
                                    Rest material machining

                                                                                                                                                    Associative job copy

                                                                                                                                                                                Copy of a job in which all parameters correspond to the parameters of the original job. A job
                                                                                                                                                                                copy is associatively linked with the original job. If a parameter is changed in the original job,
                                                                                                                                                                                then this parameter will also change in the associative job copy. Parameters cannot be
                                                                                                                                                                                edited. Exception: transformations and contours.

                                                                                                                                                    Creating an associative job copy
                                                                                                                                                                               Select the job in the joblist in the hyperMILL browser, right-click and select the Associative
                                                                                                                                                                                job copy function from the shortcut menu.
                                                                                                                                                                               Unlink the copied job and the original job: Select the copied job in the hyperMILL browser
                                                                                                                                                                                and select the Unlink associative copy function on the shortcut menu.

                                                                                                                  The Milling area dialogue

                                                                                                                                              The dialogue consists of the Definition and Milling area dialogue pages.

                                                                                                                                              On the Definition dialogue page, define the elements that belong to the milling area. On the
                                                                                                                                              Milling area dialogue page, define the name and storage location for the milling area.

                                                                                                                  Definition dialogue page

                                                                                                                  Mode

                                                                                                                  Define the mode for the milling area definition.

                                                                                                                  Surface selection: hyperMILL automatically calculates the resolution for the selected milling
                                                                                                                  areas depending on the machining tolerance. You can select a total of five surface groups
                                                                                                                  with different resolutions and stock allowances.

                                                                                                                  File: Click the Path button to select a 3DF or STL file.

                                                                                                                                 You cannot use an external polyhedron file to define the milling area for the fol-
                                                                                                                                 lowing cycles: 3D Profile Finishing, 5X Profile Finishing, 3D Z Level Finishing,
                                                                                                                                 5X Z Level Finishing, 3D Automatic Rest Machining and 5X Rest Machining.

                                                                                                                  Current selection
                                                                                                                  Group name: Specify the Surface Group's name. A surface can only be allocated to one Sur-
                                                                                                                  face Group. You assign the groups in the job definition.

                 Measuring
           Measuring the distance between two selection points on the surfaces or of two surfaces as
           well as the angle between two surfaces. To measure, left-click a location of the element that
           is to be measured (Model, Stock, Fixture, Machine model). Follow this procedure to specify
           the first point. Then, left-click again to specify the second point. The measurement results
           are shown as:

           Info two faces
           Angle (1): Angle between surface A and surface B.
           Surface distance (2): Distance between the first clicked surface (here B) to the second
           clicked point.
           Surface distance point 2 (3): Distance between the first clicked point to the second clicked
           point (here A).
           Point distance (4): Distance between two clicked points.

           Options

           Default correction list: This value will be used if it has not already been defined in hyperMILL
           (job definition, Tool tab). Numerical values (integers), variables (tool numbers) and calcula-
           tion options (such as T:No+10) may be used.

           Tool reference point ID: definition of a unique tool name (with formula support). Prerequisite
           for a correct tool change.

           Attach to: Specify whether the components are to be placed automatically (Automatic
           option). The VERICUT interface will then automatically search for the intended clamping
           position.

           Position: Specify the position manually. The name of the VERICUT element at which the
           workpieces are placed must be defined.

           Model: Close STL specifies whether a closed solid should be created for the STL files of the
           model.

           Option Close fixture STL creates a closed solid for the STL files of the clamping part.

           Closing the files can prevent display problems in VERICUT.

           Program zero: Specify whether the VERICUT interface Automatically moves the program
           zero point or whether the setting is imported from the Project template.

           This concludes the settings required to use the VERICUT interface.

4  Feature and macro technology          The feature browser
   The advantages of feature technology

Feature and macro technology

            The advantages of feature technology

                                               Feature technology processes geometry information present in the CAD model for CAM pro-
                                               gramming in a way that significantly reduces programming effort. In addition to the assigned
                                               geometry, features also contain information relevant to manufacturing, such as tolerance
                                               values or fits.
                                               The automatic derivation of manufacturing geometries makes it possible to transfer data
                                               directly from a feature to the job definition (Feature Job Connector) for use across jobs and
                                               job lists.
                                               Furthermore, Customised Process Features make it possible to define company standards
                                               for similar geometries, thus increasing programming automation even further. In this pro-
                                               cess, work processes are defined and stored as technology macros, which can be applied to
                                               similar machining tasks.
                                               Feature technology provides you with enormous potential to increase efficiency and save
                                               time in manufacturing.

            User interface

                                               The user interface of the feature module comprises
                                             · The Feature browser (Feature tab in the hyperMILL browser) with representation of the

                                                      feature lists and features,
                                               · The Feature editor (Feature dialogue) for defining feature parameters and
                                               · The Feature job connector (Feature dialogue page of the job definition) for selecting

                                                      and using features in a job.

              The feature browser

                                             The feature tab in the hyperMILL browser is known as the Feature Browser. The Feature
                                               Browser comprises
                                               · The top range with feature lists and shortcut menu functions (1),
                                               · The bottom range with feature and shortcut menu functions (2),
                                               · A toolbar with filter functions and functions to control the visibility of features (3).

           N - Number of features of feature lists / Number of visible features.            The Feature Editor

                                                                                                                        The dialogue for defining feature parameters is called the feature editor. The feature editor
                                                                                                                        comprises
                                                                                                                        · an input area with feature parameters (1),

                                                                                                                        · a toolbar for saving inputs and calling online help (3).

                                                                                                                        Feature parameters are associatively linked to the feature and can be defined by selecting
                                                                                                                        geometric elements in the CAD model. If a geometric element is changed in the CAD model,
                                                                                                                        the change is copied to the feature.
                                                                                                                        Defining feature parameters using the following geometric elements:
                                                                                                                                    Snap point, point, centre point of a circle, top / bottom of a cylinder.

                                                                                                                 General information

                                                                                                                                             Define the Name for the feature. The type is set automatically.
                                                                                                                                             If required, define a Name for the feature class and structure the work with feature classes
                                                                                                                                             and features. Features which are used to edit an area of the model, can be combined in a
                                                                                                                                             Feature class and quickly selected and re-used when creating Macros using filters.
                                                                                                                                             To allocate a feature to a Feature class, enter the name of the feature class in the Feature
                                                                                                                                             class line. The name is freely definable and may reflect a typical machining sequence, for
                                                                                                                                             example. It is displayed in the feature browser and in the macro database.

                                                                                                                 Example

                                                                                                                 Simple Hole                   <D5 Through      Multi-Axis Indexing 1>
                                                                                                                 Feature name                  <Parameter name  Feature class name>

                                                                                                                      To allocate a feature to a Feature class, open the Select feature class dialogue and
                                                                                                                 select the respective feature class. The feature type and use of the feature are displayed. If
                                                                                                                 the Check feature type option is enabled, only feature types are displayed, which correspond
                                                                                                                 to the currently selected feature.

                                                                                                                                               If the feature is linked to a macro, the link is saved in the macro database. This
                                                                                                                                               allows the Feature class parameter to be used as a filter independently of the
                                                                                                                                               model when using macros.

                                                                                                                                               This function therefore makes it easier to reuse features and feature classes
                                                                                                                                               that are already defined.

           Linking the CPF to CAD data
           To link CAD data of a model to the CPF, proceed as follows:
           1. Right-click the feature browser and open the CPF dialogue.
           2. Select New > Customised Process Feature > [CPF name]. A corresponding entry is

                 created in the lower part of the feature browser [CPF name] and all previously defined
                 geometry elements are displayed in the CPF dialogue.
           3. For Orientation 1, select the required Frame for machining.
           4. Select the hub and side surfaces of the pocket for Surfaces 1 and 2.
           5. Select the limit of the hub surface for Profiles 1.

                                                                                                                         Check slot: Enable this option if slot recognition is required.

                                                                                                                         Slot tolerance: Tolerance for the axial distance between concentric part-holes of the same
                                                                                                                         diameter. See the information in section Single Hole Recognition.

                                                                                                                         Slot as hole element: A slot is regarded as part of a hole. Part-holes are combined into one
                                                                                                                         multi-step freely defined hole, whereby the slot area is defined as a through (B).
                                                                                                                         If this option is disabled, part-holes that go through a slot (depending on the defined toler-
                                                                                                                         ance) are recognised either as Simple Holes or Sink Holes (A).

                                                                                                                         (A) Function not enabled: (1) Simple Hole, (2) Simple Hole.

                                                                                                                         (B) Function enabled: freely defined hole, consisting of three steps: cylinder (1), through (2),
                                                                                                                         cylinder (3).

           type.

           If the pockets have chamfers or fillets, the values for the corner radius (fillet) or chamfer
           angle and chamfer height parameters must be identical. It is not possible to join chamfers
           and fillets for combination.
           The individually recognized pockets, the combined pockets and the Generic Pocket are dis-
           played in the feature browser as a result of the Pocket Recognition.

           Manually combine pockets

           Generic Pockets can be manually combined either in the feature browser via the shortcut
           menu or using the colour table. The pockets must have a common edge and the same frame
           in order to be manually combined.

           Feature and macro technology              4 Use feature                                 4     Feature and macro technology  Advantages and uses
           Functions on the shortcut menu: Features                                                      Macro technology

           _________________________________________________________________________________             Macro technology
           Set feature IDs: Define new feature IDs for the selected elements, beginning with ID1.
           _________________________________________________________________________________                                         Macros link machining strategies and tools for machining characteristic geometries (= fea-
           Usage: Display the jobs in which the selected element is used in a separate window.                                       tures) and thereby considerably reduce programming expenditure during production.
           Check model: Check the consistency of the contours assigned to the job.
           hyperMILL setup: Open the dialogue for inputting the basic settings of hyperMILL.             Advantages and uses

                                                                                                                                     · Automation and recycling of workflows: Workflows can be automated and recycled
                                                                                                                                            using macros. This significantly reduces programming time, particularly when it comes
                                                                                                                                            to producing 2.5D parts.

                                                                                                                                     · Efficient macro management: Your macros reside in a macro database. This provides a
                                                                                                                                            production knowledge base that is efficiently and easily managed.

                                                                                                                                     · Updating workflows: You can modify your existing macros at any point to match user-
                                                                                                                                            specific new production requirements as they arise.

                                                                                                                                     · Higher degree of automation thanks to `intelligent' macros: Using `intelligent' macros,
                                                                                                                                            operations that were previously assigned to a feature manually can be automatically
                                                                                                                                          linked. Rules and conditions are defined to allow hyperMILL to automatically decide
                                                                                                                                            which machining will be applied. This method can therefore reduce the number of mac-
                                                                                                                                            ros needed to machine a complete model.

                                                                                                         Creating macros

                                                                                                                                     A macro includes features and job information. It is created based on a job or features

                                                                                                         Creating job-based macros
                                                                                                                                     To generate macros on a job
                                                                                                                                    1. Open the hyperMILL browser and select the Jobs tab.
                                                                                                                                     2. Highlight the job you want to associate with the macro and select Macros > New Macro
                                                                                                                                            from Job. The New Macro window opens.

                                                                                                         Creating feature-based macros
                                                                                                                                     To generate macros on a feature
                                                                                                                                    1. Open the hyperMILL browser and select the Feature tab.
                                                                                                                                     2. Highlight the feature whose information you wish to use.
                                                                                                                                     3. Right-click the entry and select New Macro from Feature .
                                                                                                                                     The New Macro dialogue box opens.

                                                                                                         The New Macro dialogue box

                                                                                                                                     Macro
                                                                                                                                     Name: The name of the source feature. This is part of the macro name. The name is written
                                                                                                                                     to the macro database when the macro is saved. The name is also used for automatic macro
                                                                                                                                     searches. The names of feature-based macros contain the prefix F; the names of job-based
                                                                                                                                     macros contain the prefix J.
                                                                                                                                     Comment: You can also enter a comment for easier identification of the macro.

                                                                                                                                                     Macro group: Each macro has to be assigned to a specific macro group. Macro
                                                                                                                                                     groups allow you to combine macros that are typical for a particular machining
                                                                                                                                                     situation, for example.

                                                                                                         Define a new macro group.

                                                                                                                 Modify a macro group.

                                                                                                         Machine group / Material group: Enable if the new macro is only to be used for one specific
                                                                                                         machine or material group.

5 Probing                             Tools
          Available machining cycles

Probing

     Available machining cycles

                                 3D Point Probing: Measure the coordinates of any 3D points to measure the accuracy of a
                                 machining job.

                                 Rectangular Probing: Measure the size and location of rectangular bosses and pockets to
                                 measure the accuracy of a machining job. Optionally, a reference tool can be adjusted and
                                 the origin set.

                                 Circular Probing: Measure the size and location of cylinders and holes to measure the accu-
                                 racy of a machining job. Optionally, a reference tool can be adjusted and the origin set.

                                 Axis dependent Probing: Measure the location of points depending on the X, Y and Z axis of
                                 the machining frame to measure the accuracy of a machining job. Optionally, a reference
                                 tool can be adjusted and the origin set.

     3D Point Probing

     Tools     Permissible tool types are touch probe tools. The geometry parameters correspond to the
     Contours  geometry parameters of the lollipop tool type. Possible tool reference points are Tip and
               Centre.

               Probing mode
               Automatic (1): Select when the probing direction is to be detected automatically.
               Manual (2): The probing direction can be set manually for individual probing points. To do
               this, activate under Contour attributes the required points and the Reverse option.

               Contour selection / faces

                                     Select points and surfaces. The points to be measured must be located on
                                     the selected surfaces.

6 Turning        Definition

Turning

     Available machining cycles

                                 Roughing: Roughing of a turning stock of any shape axially or radially to contour.

                                 Contour Parallel Turning: roughing of turning stock of any shape in parallel to contour.
                                 Finishing: Contour parallel finishing of workpieces of any shape based on a preceding rough-
                                 ing operation.
                                 Rollfeed Turning: Machining of workpieces by rolling the tool insert on the component con-
                                 tour, ensuring a very high surface quality.

                                 3X simultaneous Roughing: Roughing of workpieces with a simultaneous swivel axis.

                                 3X simultaneous Finishing: Finishing of workpieces with a simultaneous swivel axis.

                                 Groove Turning: Axial roughing of workpieces with grooves or shoulders.

                                 Grooving: Radial Roughing of workpieces with grooves and shoulders.

                                 Groove Finishing: Radial finishing of turning workpieces with grooves or shoulders.
                                 Face Groove Turning: Radial roughing of workpieces with axial oriented grooves or shoul-
                                 ders. The tools used normally have three cutting edges.
                                 Face Groove Plunging: Axial roughing of workpieces with axial oriented grooves or shoul-
                                 ders. The tools used normally have three cutting edges.

                                 Face Groove Finishing: Finishing of workpieces with axial oriented grooves or shoulders.

                                 Parting: Radial machining to separate the component from the bar stock, optionally with
                                 chamfer. Parting off can be done on the front or at the back of the workpiece.
                                 Thread Cutting: Creation of single or multiple start, cylindrical or conical, external and inter-
                                 nal threads with constant pitch. Infeed can be performed either with constant chip section or
                                 with constant X value.

     Definition

                 Turning is a production process for manufacturing rotationally symmetrical internal and
                 external surfaces by removing wood from turning stock of any shape. The external shape of
                 a workpiece is created by using the Outside option, and the internal shape by using the
                 Inside option.

                 The millTURN module allows for the combination of milling and turning tasks in a job list.

                 Stockmodel for subsequent machining tasks: As with milling jobs, a stockmodel can also be
                 generated for subsequent turning operations (resulting stock).

                 NC files: The NC files created with the millTURN module can be used for both milling and
                 turning tasks.

                     allel to the turning axis and 90° is perpendicular to the turning axis.

                     Steep areas: Only the steep areas of the defined contour are machined (2).
                     Flat areas: Only the flat areas of the defined contour are machined (3).

                     Contours: Define contours for turning operations. These may correspond to the contour of

                     Start point / endpoint: define the start and end points for machining, either by selecting a                              rounded or chamfered. Define the chamfer length (2) and the chamfer angle (3) for chamfer-

                     The icon changes (2). Enter the required value.

                     required factor directly.

                       Cutting speed

                     Cutting profile. The values are displayed for each contour segment.

           Strategy

                     Strategy

                     The machining strategy is determined by the parting tool definition. If the parting insert posi-
                     tion on the tool is left, front face is automatically enabled as a strategy (1); if the position is
                     right, back face is activated as a strategy (2). If the parting insert position on the tool is neu-
                     tral, the strategy can be chosen freely (3). In this case, the parameter front angle of the insert
                     is not available.

7 Drilling
          Contours

Drilling

     Available machining cycles

                                 Centering: Enables centrings with various parameters.

                                 Simple Drilling: Machining of Simple Holes in one infeed.

                                 Drilling with Chip Beak: Machining of Simple Holes in several drilling strokes.

                                 Drilling with Pecking: Machining of Simple Holes with rapid retract to the clearance distance
                                 between each drilling stroke.

                                 Optimised deep Hole Drilling: Machining of holes with feedrate optimisation for cross holes
                                 or breakthroughs.

                                 Reaming: Reboring to improve the quality of the surface when chip thickness is reduced.

                                 Tapping: Drilling of threads with various parameters.
                                 Boring: Drilling with a boring bar for large drilling diameters. Input parameters similar to Sim-
                                 ple Hole.

                                 Helical Drilling: Machining of circular pockets with helical stepdown and horizontal grooving
                                 on the pocket floor. Roughing, grooving on pocket floor, finishing and chamfering can be car-
                                 ried out in one job.

                                 Thread milling: Using a helical stepdown, this cycle produces single and multiple inside and
                                 outside threads with a definable chamfer. A hole must have been predrilled for internal
                                 threads.

                                 Circular Pocket: Machining of holes in parallel to the contour, with specifiable machining
                                 direction using climb milling or conventional milling.

                                 Gun Drilling: Drilling very deep holes with a long tool with small diameter. This requires a
                                 previously drilled hole of the same diameter as the hole to be created by Gun Drilling.

                                 5X Helical Drilling (MAXX Machining): This cycle produces circular holes through helical
                                 toolpaths. The tool is executed in a 5-axis manner with a given lead and tilt angle.

     Tool

                    For information on tool definitions, see section Defining a tool in the hyperMILL browser.

                    The following applies to all drilling cycles that support the parameter Tip angle compensa-
                    tion:

                    When using stepped tools with multiple reference points (for example, reference point 1 = 0
                    and reference point 2 = 25), this option should not be enabled.

     Contours

                    Define the drilling strategy, contour selection for the holes and the vertical machining area
                    (top and depth) of the holes.

                    Drilling mode

                    The drill cycles can be used in all drilling modes. The Turning mode is available
                    for turning jobs with a rotating spindle.

                    2D Drilling: The direction of the drill holes is always aligned with the Z axis of the defined
                    frame system. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature definition. All drill
                    holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.

                    2D multi-axis drilling: the direction of any number of drillings can be aligned with the different
                    frames/planes. For infeed movements in XY direction, a relative clearance (automatically
                    calculated for each frame) can be defined. The conditions for collision-proof linking move-
                    ments between the planes can be made available using the Lateral clearance and Globally
                    highest point parameters. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.

7-2                 hyperMILL
           Drilling                                     7 Contours                                                           7 Drilling          2D multi index drilling
           2D Drilling                                                                                                                 Contours
                        5X Drilling: The direction of the drill holes is aligned with the normals of the selected surfaces
                        or with the selected lines. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature defini-                         The direction of the drill hole is determined by the Z axis of the defined frame (-

                        The following applies to multi-axis indexing:

                        1. in Drilling mode: the frame specifies the machining direction. The linking movements
                              between the frames are controlled by the postprocessor.

                        2. in 5X Drilling mode: several sides can be machined in one job. The linking movements
                              between the machining sides are collision tested and are executed as 5X simultaneous
                              movements. A machine is required that supports this type of movement.

                        For further information, see section Settings.
                        Turning: With this option, turning jobs can be carried out with a rotating spindle and fixed
                        tool. The machining direction is defined by the Z axis of the frame. The drill position is always
                        located in the centre point of the workpiece being turned.
                        Frame dependent: Available for the 5X Helical Drilling cycle. The direction of the drill holes is
                        aligned with the Z axis of the defined frame system. When using features, the frame system
                        is part of the feature definition. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.

           Circular Pocket

                                       For this cycle, you can define the contours as circles (or points) or lines.
                                       Horizontal stepover factor: Infeed in the XY plane is defined as a factor of the tool diameter

           Optimised deep Hole Drilling

                                       Drilling with an initial stockmodel, a stockmodel update and start drilling strategies as well as
                                       crosshole and breakthrough drilling. Optimised deep Hole Drilling breaks down all move-

                     Hole collision avoidance A/B

8 2D machining                 Contour selection
          General Information

2D machining

     Available machining cycles

                                 Pocket Milling: Machining perpendicular pocket walls and adaptive pockets with automatic
                                 island recognition and calculation of rest material areas.

                                 Contour Milling: Milling open and closed 2D contours with optional path compensation and
                                 different approach and retract strategies. Rest material areas can be calculated.

                                 Contour Milling on 3D Model: Milling open and closed contours with collision control, optional
                                 stop faces and automatic approach and retract strategies.

                                 T-slot cutting on 3D model: Roughing and finishing of T-slots along plane contours. Different
                                 axial infeed modes allow a free definition of Z infeed. Multiple tool reference points ensure
                                 precise milling results. Collision control and infeed movements based on a 3D model.
                                 Chamfer Milling on 3D Model: Machining of prismatic workpieces. It is possible to differenti-
                                 ate between the Modelled chamfer and Deburr / chamfer sharp edges machining strategies.

                                 Inclined Contouring: Machining same as for Contour Milling, but with inclined pocket wall.

                                 Inclined pocketing: Machining same as for pocket milling, but with inclined pocket wall.

                                 Rectangular pocket: Machining rectangular pockets in parallel to the contour with specifiable
                                 machining direction using climb milling or conventional milling.

                                 Rest Machining: Machining rest material areas left after pocket or Contour Milling.

                                 Face Milling: Roughing of larger surfaces with parallel cuts within one or more contours,
                                 optionally with several steps in Z direction.

                                 Playback Milling: Milling on tool paths, manually generated with mouse interaction in a plane.
                                 Plunge Milling: Guided by a contour, the cycle generates a Plunge Milling toolpath. Possibil-
                                 ity to perform collision control and stock update.

     General Information

                                 If workpiece-specific parameters (top, bottom, clearance distance, contours) are entered in
                                 the drawing, they can be interactively transferred from this drawing.

                                 Adjust the existing default values in the first operation to a joblist, if necessary, in order to
                                 coordinate, for example, the top to the stock size. The modified values are transferred for all
                                 subsequent operations of the joblist.

     Tools

                               For more information on selecting the tool and defining tool parameters, see chap. Defining
                               a tool in the hyperMILL browser.

     Contours

                               Define machining contours, the vertical machining area and cycle-specific contour parame-
                               ters.

     Contour selection

                                 The following can be selected as 2D machining contours: points (drilling only), arcs, circles,
                                 reference lines, curves and curves of surfaces. Several contours or holes can be machined
                                 in one job. The number of selected contours is displayed.

     Visualisation

                               Selected contours (2) are shown in the model at the Z level of the defined top (1) and bottom
                               (3). Depending on the current cycle, the contour directions are also shown. The contour list
                               in the dialogue box shows other parameters such as start, end and plunge.

                         3D mode: In 3D mode, use the milling area to define the CAD model's machining area (see
                         the Setup dialogue page). This also means it has already been checked for collisions. For
                         more information on the milling area dialogue box, see chap. The Milling area dialogue.
                         You can also generate a stock (see the Setup dialogue page). This can also be used for
                         stock update.
                         In addition to the tool tip, you can check the holder and shaft for collisions. For more informa-
                         tion on tool checks, see chap. Check tool.
                         Stock mode: in this mode, the outermost contour is defined as the stock section contour.
                         Contours lying inside are considered islands. Machining is always performed from the out-
                         side in.

                         Path direction
                         Select the climb milling or conventional milling option for the tool cutting mode. The cutting
                         mode relates to tools rotating clockwise.

                         Adaptive pocket parameters: options for adjusting feedrates and infeed under full cut behav-
                         iour conditions.

           Parameters

                         Define machining parameters.
                         For information on the parameters:

                         Vertical stepdown, horizontal stepover factor  see section Infeed
                         XY allowance, Z allowance                      see section Allowance
                         Clearance distance, clearance plane            see section Clearance

                         Retract mode
                         Clearance plane: the tool retracts to the clearance plane after each plane has been
                         machined.
                         Lead-in keep position: the tool plunges to the next deepest plane at the current position after
                         each machined plane. This reduces machining times.
                         Lead-in reposition: the tool plunges to the next deepest plane at the current position after
                         each machined plane.

                         Toolpath fillets
                         The toolpaths in the plane can be smoothed.
                         Fillet radius: Abrupt changes in direction within the cutting toolpaths are rounded with the
                         specified radius (2).
                         Radius for horizontal infeed: the horizontal infeed between the tool paths is rounded with the
                         horizontal infeed radius (1).
                         Fillet all toolpaths: model contour corners are rounded with the radius defined above, with
                         the result that the machining contour deviates from the model contour at the corners (3).

           Chamfer Milling on 3D Model

                                       The cycle facilitates safe and rapid machining of prismatic workpieces. It is possible to differ-
                                       entiate between the Modelled chamfer and Deburr / chamfer sharp edges machining strate-
                                       gies.

           Tool

                         Only chamfered cutters are permitted for machining.

           Contours

                         See the information in section Contours.

           Machining Strategy

                                       Chamfer mode
                                       Modelled chamfer (1): The height of the chamfer is defined by the model geometry.
                                       Deburr / chamfer sharp edges (2): The height of the chamfer is defined on the Parameters
                                       dialogue page.

                                                                                                                                                            step is defined for the Vertical stepdown. The chamfer height specifies the number of
                                                                                                                                                            infeeds.
