9 3D machining
          3D Collision check

3D machining

     Available machining cycles

                                 Arbitrary Stock Roughing: Z constant stock removal of pre-fabricated blanks of any shape
                                 with the option of stock model update. Machining proceeds parallel to the specified contour
                                 or parallel to axis.

                                 Optimised Roughing: Roughing and rest roughing of any workpieces. Calculate toolpaths for
                                 standard pocket shapes such as rectangular and circular pockets. The model geometry and
                                 stock model geometry will be taken into consideration to calculate highly efficient toolpaths
                                 and reduce direction changes ("high speed cutting"). Machine remaining rest material areas
                                 based on the generated "resulting stock".
                                 Profile Finishing: Allows multi-surface, collision-free milling with different guide curve strate-
                                 gies; optional slope-dependent machining. An XY optimised strategy is offered for the X and
                                 Y machining profiles.

                                 Z Level Finishing: Z constant finishing with optional slope-dependent machining. By adapting
                                 the vertical stepdown values to the surface flow especially for steep surfaces, unnecessary
                                 fine infeed increments are avoided and an optimal line distance is thus guaranteed.

                                 Shape level finishing: Z-Level machining for steep areas. Optionally, plane machining can be
                                 replaced by cuts parallel to any shape.

                                 Iso Machining: The milling paths follow the ISO lines (U, V) so that they are optimally
                                 adapted to the surface curve.

                                 Free Path Milling: Milling of free defined 3D contours. Multiple vertical stepdown and ramped
                                 transition between milling paths are possible.

                                 Plane Machining: Face Milling of planar surfaces with pocket strategy. Automatic plane level
                                 detection or manual selection of surfaces. The stockmodel can be used for trimming.

                                 Complete Finishing: Z Level Finishing with automatic pocket-shaped machining of flat areas.

                                 Equidistant Finishing: Finishing with constant infeed on surface; particularly suitable for high-
                                 speed milling. Machining takes place equidistantly within a closed guide curve or flowing
                                 between two guide curves.

                                 Form Pocket: Finishing of pockets with free-form floor.

                                 Pencil Milling: Automatic detection and machining of grooves.
                                 Automatic Rest Machining: Remachining of separate rest material areas left during a finish-
                                 ing cycle.

                                 Rework Machining: Machining of pre-calculated toolpaths from a reference job where the
                                 toolpaths could not be machined due to detected collisions. For the rework machining, a dif-
                                 ferent tool is applied to avoid the previously detected collision areas from the reference job.

                                 Rib / Groove Machining: Roughing and finishing of ribs and grooves or limited groups thereof
                                 in one job for side surfaces and floor areas respectively.
                                 Cutting Edge: Optimised machining of cutting edges using curve-based pre-roughing (strat-
                                 egy: manual curve) in 3D mode, followed by rest machining in 2D mode (strategy: reference
                                 cycle).

     3D Collision check

                                 Collision monitoring is assured by the following factors:

                                 1. Milling area/turning area: 3D collision models are the part of the CAD model defined as
                                        a milling area or turning area (also see section Milling area, Turning area, Clamping
                                        area).

                                 2. Frame: The orientation of the frame system determines which of the surfaces included
                                        in a machining area can be milled. The system machines only those surfaces which are
                                        visible from the tool axis.

                                 3. Clearance plane and distance: These parameters limit the areas for rapid tool move-
                                        ments (see section Safety).

                         Retract mode                                                                                                       Boundary

                         The retract mode defines the Z level where the system executes horizontal infeed move-                                            Define the machining area, the edge behaviour of the tool at the machining boundaries (tool
                         ments. The mode set is valid for all machining directions (incl. approach, retract and return                                     reference), the plunge point for the machining.
                         movement macros) and for the profiles machined with them. Exception: Machining in zigzag
                         mode without return macro.                                                                                                        Different methods are available for defining boundaries, depending on the machining cycle.
                                                                                                                                                           Explanations are provided in the respective machining cycle sections
                         Clearance distance (1): all retract and infeed movements are executed via the clearance dis-
                         tance. Starting and end positions of an infeed movement in rapid are displaced in Z direction
                         in order to guarantee a collision-free linear infeed movement. The clearance distance is
                         added to these positions.

                         Clearance plane (2): all retract and infeed movements are executed via the clearance plane.

                                                                                                                                            Subdivision of the machining areas

                                                                                                                                                                        The subdivision of the workpiece into different machining areas uses the following criteria:
                                                                                                                                                                        · Geometric criteria: surface curvature, main direction, characteristic extension, position

                                                                                                                                                                               in space of the surface
                                                                                                                                                                        · Suitable tool type
                                                                                                                                                                        · Optimum milling strategy.

                                                                                                                                            Independent machining areas

                                                                                                                                                                        Efficient machining with short machining times and minimized finishing times can often only
                                                                                                                                                                        be carried out if the workpiece has been subdivided carefully into different machining areas
                                                                                                                                                                        (particular surfaces, group of surfaces).

                                                                                                                                                                        If independent machining areas with the same machining direction, the same machining
                                                                                                                                                                        strategy, and the same tool with the same orientation of the frame are detected during clas-
                                                                                                                                                                        sification into milling areas, these areas can be machined together in one cycle.

                                                                                                                                                                        In order to avoid steps and tool marks, the machining areas should not overlap and should
                                                                                                                                                                        not be too close together. If this is not possible, the boundaries should be combined into one
                                                                                                                                                                        machining area.

           Strategy parameters                                                                                                                             To avoid unwanted nose-diving of the tool, the boundary area and the edges of
                                                                                                                                                           the milling surfaces must not contain any surfaces the tool cannot access (slots,
                                       Different strategy parameters are available, depending on the machining cycle. Explanations                         for example).
                                       are provided in the respective machining cycle sections.
                                                                                                                                                           Milling surfaces must not contain any double or superimposed surfaces.

           High Performance Roughing                                                                                                            Reposition

                                    Introduction                                                                                                The following applies to the two strategies Opening cut and Side mill only:
                                       With the High Performance Roughing option, OPEN MIND provides an additional roughing
                                       technology that is characterised by the following features:                                              Safety (1): axial movement (in the Z direction) away from the plane currently being
                                       · Constant load on the tool and machine during the entire machining sequence.                            machined. Default value: Clearance distance * 0.1.
                                       · Feedrates that are adjusted dynamically to the machining situation
                                       · Machining is always performed using climb milling.                                                     Feedrate: Value for the maximum achievable feedrate for all movements to reposition the

           Tools                                                                                                                               Profile Finishing

           Profile Finishing                                                                                                                                      When the X axis and Y axis options are used, the X or Y axis of the frame is used as the
                                                                                                                                                                  guide curve.
                                       Allows multi-surface, collision-free milling with different guide curve strategies. Selected
                                       areas can be machined in slope mode.                                                                                       With all the other options, the guide curves are freely definable, which allows the milling
                                                                                                                                                                  paths to be optimally adapted to the surface.

                                                                                                                                                                  Machining angle: Enter the rotation angle required for machining.

           Tools                                                                                                                                                  The machining and infeed directions are based on the guide curves. This setting is the
                                                                                                                                                                  standard setting.
                               The following cutter types can be used: ball mill, end mill, bullnose end mill and lollipop.
                                                                                                                                                                  Reverse direction
                               Exceptions: Profile Finishing in scallop height mode only supports ball mills,                                                     Both the milling and infeed direction can be customised in order to make optimal adjust-
                               and slope-dependent machining only supports bullnose endmills and ballmills.                                                       ments to the milling paths to the surface.
                                                                                                                                                                  Milling path: Reverses the machining direction.
                               When using tapered tools, collision avoidance is possible by taking into account the conical                                       Horizontal stepover: Reverses the infeed direction.
                               shape of the tool for the toolpaths.
                                                                                                                                                                                 Via the selected directions the starting point of machining is defined as well.
                               For further information on selecting a tool and defining tool parameters, see section Defining
                               a tool.                                                                                                                            X axis, Y axis
                                                                                                                                                                  The machining area is to be limited via a boundary. The guide curve for machining is the X
           Strategy                                                                                                                                               axis. In the default setting, the first milling path runs in the positive X direction and the first
                                                                                                                                                                  infeed movement is executed to the left of this, that is, in the positive Y direction.
                               Infeed strategy
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        hyperMILL
                               The following are defined in the infeed strategy area:
                               · The profile of the tool movements via a profile definition (standard profiles, free pro-

                                     files).

                               · The type of cut for the tool (Ascending, Descending, Ascending and descending)

                               · The infeed mode between the end point of the first milling path and the start point of the
                                     following milling path.

                               The options that are available in the Profile definition, Type of cut and Infeed mode areas are
                               explained in the following sections using examples.

           Profile definition

                               If a profile has not been defined, the defined boundary (strategy: Boundary curve ) or the
                               boundary for the defined milling surfaces (strategy: Milling surfaces) is used automatically as
                               the profile.

                                                                                                                                                      The machining of surfaces with a large slope angle frequently leads to unsatisfactory results

           Tools                                                                                                                                  Iso Machining
                                                                                                                                                                 To machine neighbouring surfaces within a boundary, the surfaces must meet without any
           Iso Machining                                                                                                                                         gaps and flowing transitions of the ISO lines are required at the common edge curves.
                                                                                                                                                                 Jumps or changes in direction are not permitted.
                                       This cycle is primarily used for the exact machining of individual or less continuous surfaces.                           If two surfaces border each other with ISO parameters that flow into each other, but whose U
                                       The milling paths follow the course of ISO lines (U, V) so that they are optimally adapted to                             and V lines are defined in an opposing manner (1), the ISO lines of the second surface are
                                       the surface flow.                                                                                                         automatically adapted to those of the first surface (2).

                                       Several neighbouring surfaces can be machined in one job step if a flowing transition exists
                                       between the ISO lines of these surfaces and the surfaces are not trimmed. Above all, excel-
                                       lent milling profiles result for rounded surfaces.

                                       Trimmed surfaces within the machining area will not be machined coherently. Each surface
                                       will be machined individually.

Plane Machining                                                                                                                                                                                 Clearance

                            · Face Milling of planar surfaces with pocket strategy.                                                                                                             Clearance plane and clearance distance apply in the direction of the Z axis of the current

                                                                                                                                                                                                distance, infeed takes place as rapid in the Z direction. Below the clearance distance infeed
                                                                                                                                                                                                takes place at the Z feedrate.

                                                                                                                                                        Defining the tool parameters  see section Defining a tool

                                                                                                                                                        Slope dependent machining
                                                                                                                                                        Off: No slope dependent machining takes place.
                                                                                                                                                        All areas: Steep as well as flat areas are machined.
                                                                                                                                                        Slope angle: The delimitation of steep and flat areas is determined by the slope angle. The
                                                                                                                                                        values between 10 and 80 degrees are useful.
                                                                                                                                                        Steep areas: Only steep areas whose surface gradient is greater than the defined slope
                                                                                                                                                        angle are machined.
                                                                                                                                                        Flat areas: Only flat areas whose surface gradient is smaller than the defined slope angle
                                                                                                                                                        are machined.

                                                                                                                                                                       Depending on the slope angle, you can thus further limit the machining area in
                                                                                                                                                                       addition to the selected boundary.

                                                                                                                                                        Smooth overlap: Only available for slope-dependent machining. Enable if you want the tool-
                                                                                                                                                        paths of flat and steep areas to overlap. The overlap (1) ensures a very high level of surface
                                                                                                                                                        quality in the transition area between flat and steep surfaces. (2) Transition area activated,
                                                                                                                                                        (3) Transition area not activated.
                                                                                                                                                        The overlap area is visualised in the graphic for illustrative purposes only. This area is not
                                                                                                                                                        graphically highlighted in the model.
                                                                                                                                                        (4) 3D Profile Finishing, (5) 3D Z Level Shape Finishing

                         permissible value for the fillet radius corresponds to the tool radius.

                                        Interior corners are no longer machined completely, resulting in rest material.

           Form Pocket

                                       Finishing of pockets with free-form floor.

                                       Here, the pocket contour is automatically determined based on a reference plane (R-PLN).
                                       Within this contour, the milling paths are calculated parallel to the contour from the inside
                                       outward and are projected onto the pocket floor. In this way, free-form surfaces of the male
                                       and female moulds of a deep-drawing tool can be produced within the pocket geometry of
                                       the supporting base in one work step.

                                                                                                                                                             Conventional milling / Climb milling: To achieve good results during styrofoam milling,

           Tools                                                                                                                    Automatic Rest Machining

           Standard

                          There is no optimisation when machining the rest material. This strategy corresponds to
                          standard machining in earlier hyperMILL versions. Machining can be non-slope-dependent
                          or slope-dependent.

           Cavities and open areas

                                       Both cavities and open (accessible) areas are machined. Slope-dependent machining is
                                       automatically activated.

                          Machining mode

                          Slope dependent machining - All areas: Steep areas in cavities always undergo Z-constant
                          machining, while flat areas in cavities (grounds) are always machined parallel to the contour.
                          Steep and flat areas can be machined using the Normal, Parallel or Z-Level strategies.

                          Slope dependent machining - Steep areas: Steep areas in cavities undergo Z-constant
                          machining. Steep areas within openly accessible areas can be machined using the Z-Level,
                          Parallel and Normal strategies.

                          Slope dependent machining - Flat areas: Cavities are not machined! Flat areas within openly
                          accessible areas can be machined using the Parallel or Normal strategies.

                                                                                                                                    Cavity depth (1): Available for the Cavities and open areas and Only cavities strategies.
                                                                                                                                    Defines the depth from which the machining mode switches to cavity mode.
                                                                                                                                    Calculation method:
                                                                                                                                    R5 Radius reference tool
                                                                                                                                    R1.5 Radius machining tool

           Only cavities

                          Only cavities are machined. Slope-dependent machining is automatically activated.                         Example of use

                          Machining mode                                                                                            If the value for the cavity depth (1.45 and 3.36) is larger than the value defined under
                                                                                                                                    machining mode (1.4 for (1) and 3.3 for (2)), machining will take place in cavity mode.
                          Slope dependent machining - All areas: Steep areas in cavities always undergo Z-constant
                          machining, while flat areas in cavities (grounds) are always machined parallel to the contour.

                          Slope dependent machining - Steep areas: Steep areas in cavities undergo Z-constant
                          machining. Flat areas are not machined.

                         Oneway (1): Machining is always performed in the same direction.

1 Appendix                                                                                          Overview

Appendix

      Application Settings

      Overview

                The Application Settings program allows you to configure your OPEN MIND software. The
                following settings are possible:

      Area of application

                                  For: Shows the area of application for the application settings.
                                  <System>: The settings apply to all users of the system.
                                  [Username]: The settings apply to the current user.

      Language

                Shows all languages registered for this program version. Selecting the relevant language
                switches the language for hyperMILL and auxiliary programs (hyperVIEW, OPEN MIND Tool
                Database etc.), but the hyperCAD-S setting remains unchanged.

                [Language]: Displays the language configured for the current user.
                [Language] <System>: Displays the language configured for all users of the system.
                After this option is selected, the active user returns to using the currently active system lan-
                guage. When the system language is changed, the language is also changed again for this
                user.

      Registered applications

                                  List of registered applications.
                                  Programs registered for all users are displayed in gray. Unless the Application Settings pro-
                                  gram is started with administrator privileges, it will not be possible to edit or delete these
                                  entries.
                                  Programs that are registered for the currently active user are displayed in black and can be
                                  edited and/or deleted by the currently active user.
                                  New: Add new application to the applications list.
                                  Edit / Delete: Edit or remove the existing application from list of registered applications.
                                  Key: Name used by OPEN MIND programs to start the application.
                                  Name: User-defined application name.
                                  Program: Complete path name under which the application is installed.
                                  Arguments: Users can enter additional parameters.

                               Show Eutron and Sentinel hardlocks
                                  Shows the Eutron and Sentinel dongles used on the computer.

                          ment are updated immediately in the preview.

           Structure View                                                                                                                                         Borders

                                       The right area, known as the structure view, is used to edit a report layout. In this area, the
                                       user can select an element to edit its properties, as well as add new elements if necessary.

                                       The context inside the report dataset, which is referenced e.g. when inserting placeholders,
                                       appears above the tree.

                                       Logical elements, such as placeholders and loops, are highlighted blue in the tree view while
                                       visible elements are displayed in normal black.

                                       It is possible to make direct changes to the properties of visible and logical elements in the
                                       lower Properties dialogue.

           Properties Dialogue

                                       The properties of the various elements in the structure of a report layout can be adjusted in
                                       the Properties dialogue.

hyperMILL                  13-3                                                                                                         13-4                                               hyperMILL
           Appendix                                                1 ReportDesigner                       1 Appendix                Tables, rows and columns
           Text Areas and Properties                                                                                ReportDesigner
                                                                                                    13-5
                                               Margins                                                          Tables, rows and columns
                                               CSS styles
                                               Element properties                                                                           Tables are an important visible element for the display of values in a report. Tables are suit-
                                                                                                                                            able to graphically structure the overall output of a report, as well as to list the individual val-
hyperMILL                                                                                                                                   ues of a dataset.

                                                                                                                                            Tables (table) are divided into an optional header area (thead) and one or more table body
                                                                                                                                            areas (tbody).

                                                                                                                                            The header area can be used to e.g. display the headings of a tabular list, while the values
                                                                                                                                            can be specified as a placeholder using a loop (xsl:for-each) in the rows (tr) and columns (td)
                                                                                                                                            of a table body.
                                                                                                                                            In this way, you can generate a tabular list of the used tools with the respective tool proper-
                                                                                                                                            ties.
                                                                                                                                            Another function of tables is to specify the display areas inside a page. To do so, the dimen-
                                                                                                                                            sions of the columns are specified explicitly, e.g. a table with a width of 100% can be divided
                                                                                                                                            into three columns with widths of 25%, 50% and 25%. It is alternatively possible to specify
                                                                                                                                            widths in pixels using the abbreviation px. In this way, the user can divide the page into sev-
                                                                                                                                            eral display areas and position images or text ranges as needed. Further structure elements
                                                                                                                                            can then be hierarchically created inside the display areas.

                                                                                                                Simple and Numbered Lists

                                                                                                                                            The ReportDesigner provides functions for ordered and unordered lists. The difference is
                                                                                                                                            simply in the numbering of the list elements, i.e. ordered lists are automatically numbered as
                                                                                                                                            1, 2, 3, ... or A, B, C, ...

                                                                                                                Images and Graphics

                                                                                                                                            Image files in the GIF, PNG and JPG formats can be integrated into the report layout in the
                                                                                                                                            ReportDesigner as static images (img). Images can also be dynamically embedded for tools.
                                                                                                                                            This means that images of the tools are automatically created during report generation and
                                                                                                                                            shown in the report output.

                                                                                                                                            The difference between static and dynamic images is that the paths to static images do not
                                                                                                                                            change and they can therefore be fixed in the report layout. Dynamic images relate to a spe-
                                                                                                                                            cific job or tool, for example, and are read from the report dataset and entered in the report
                                                                                                                                            layout using a placeholder.

                                                                                                                Logical Elements

                                                                                                                                            In addition to visible elements, which are used to format the report output, the ReportDe-
                                                                                                                                            signer also provides a range of logical elements, which can be used to embed the data from
                                                                                                                                            a job list or tool dataset in the report output.

                                                                                                                                            Note that the underlying dataset of e.g. a job list is hierarchically structured in its own right.
                                                                                                                                            The ReportDesigner helps the user insert placeholders and loops by only making properties
                                                                                                                                            and possible loops belonging to the current data element available for selection, depending
                                                                                                                                            on the context.

                                                                                                                                         Placeholders

                                                                                                                                            Job lists, jobs, tools and other data elements have specific properties such as designation,
                                                                                                                                            numbering, length, colour etc.

                                                                                                                                            Depending on the context in the report dataset, the user can insert individual properties of,
                                                                                                                                            for example, a job into the report layout using a placeholder (xsl:value-of). The possible job
                                                                                                                                            properties are made available in the selection dialogue, and are then applied to the place-
                                                                                                                                            holder's select attribute.

                                                                                                                                            Placeholders can be inserted from the Insert > Value Of ... menu item.

                                                                                                                                            The possible attributes, in this case those of the tool, are selected depending on the context
                                                                                                                                            in the report dataset.
                                                                                                                                            Sometimes it may be necessary to specifically access properties of the superordinate ele-
                                                                                                                                            ment or other elements in the report dataset, or formatting functions. The ReportDesigner
                                                                                                                                            uses the xpath query language for this purpose, which means that the user can enter arbi-

                                                                                                          13-6                                                hyperMILL
           Appendix          1 ReportDesigner                                                                                     1 Appendix                                                                                     Conditions
           Logical Elements                                                                                                                 ReportDesigner

                             trary other xpath expressions in the select attribute with knowledge of the structure of the               Conditions
                             dataset.
                                                                                                                                                            Inside the loop, it may be necessary to only display certain elements, for example jobs with a
                             xsl and xpath offer an enormous range of options, which are not described in further detail                                    particular property. To achieve this, the user can use a condition to filter the output. The
                             here. A number of tutorials and a wide range of documentation are available on the internet.                                   Insert > Condition menu item allows such filters to be inserted.

                             Loops and Repetition
                             Every report dataset is built around a hierarchical structure. A job list, for example, consists
                             of a list of individual jobs and an additional list of used tools.

                             A list of jobs can be visualised in a number of ways, e.g. as an overview in a table or as a list
                             of pages, each of which shows an individual job.

                             For display, it is first necessary to create a loop to cover all jobs in the job list. In the first
                             example case, this loop is used to display the table rows.

                             In the second case, each iteration of the loop displays an entire page. Loops are available
                             under the Insert > For all ... menu item.

                             Because tables with a loop structure are required in many cases, the Tools menu contains                   Other functions
                             the Dynamic table menu item to bring these common steps together in one place.
                                                                                                                                                                    The Tools menu in the ReportDesigner contains a few special functions for the calculation of
                             The following structure is inserted:                                                                                                   certain values.

                                                                                                                                        MinTlength

                                                                                                                                                            The MinTlength function is used to output the shortest length of a tool in a job list. If a tool is
                                                                                                                                                            used several times, only the tool with the shortest required length will be used. This prevents
                                                                                                                                                            tools from being output multiple times.

                                                                                                                                        Zmax-Zmin

                                                                                                                                                            Output of the relative and axial heights of a tool path (z-height).

                                                                                                                                                                    · Internet Explorer 8
                                                                                                                                                                    · MS Office 2007 or higher
                                                                                                                                                                    · Windows XP, Windows Vista, Windows 7
